concepts.title: Textual and Tabular Presentation
concepts.definition: Data can be presented in text, where figures are woven into sentences and comparisons stay hard to grasp, or in tables -- the master device of presentation, with stub for the rows, caption for the columns, and cells holding the figures in compact, comparable form.
concepts.key_idea: Prose hides figures, tables display them -- stub, caption and body make data speak at a glance.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest104.txt textual tabular sections (textual presentation, tabular presentation, parts of a table, stub caption body head note footnote)
question_patterns: distinguish textual and tabular presentation of data
in class 11 presentation of data: name the parts of a table and their functions
what is the stub of a table
why is tabulation preferred to textual description for large data
construct a table for the given information with proper caption
explain the role of head note and footnotes in a table

solution_steps.explain: Textual presentation suits few figures; tables compress many figures into comparable rows and columns.
Give a title, place row descriptions in the stub and column descriptions in the caption, and fill the body with figures.
Head notes clarify units, footnotes qualify entries, and the source note records where data came from.

concepts.title: Diagrammatic Presentation: Bar Diagrams and Pie Charts
concepts.definition: Diagrams translate figures into pictures. Bar diagrams of one dimension compare magnitudes through length -- simple, multiple, component and percentage bars; the pie chart slices a circle so that each component's angle shows its share of a total of 360 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Lengths compare, circles share -- bar diagrams for magnitudes, pie charts for parts of a whole.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest104.txt diagram sections (bar diagram simple multiple component percentage, pie chart, degrees of the circle, merits of diagrams)
question_patterns: explain the types of bar diagrams with examples
in class 11 presentation of data: how is a pie chart constructed
calculate the angle for a given component in a pie diagram
when is a component bar diagram preferred to multiple bars
state the merits and limitations of diagrammatic presentation
draw a simple bar diagram for the given data

solution_steps.explain: Divide the component value by the total to get its fraction of the whole.
Multiply the share by 360 to obtain the angle the slice subtends at the centre.

concepts.title: Frequency Diagrams: Histogram, Polygon and Ogive
concepts.definition: Frequency distributions get their own pictures: the histogram joins adjacent rectangles over class intervals; the frequency polygon connects mid-points of the rectangles; and the ogive plots cumulative frequencies, rising to the total. These graphs reveal the shape of a distribution at sight.
concepts.key_idea: Rectangles for classes, lines for mid-points, curves for cumulative counts -- the distribution's silhouette in three graphs.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest104.txt frequency curve sections (histogram, frequency polygon, frequency curve, ogive cumulative frequency curve, uses of each)
question_patterns: in class 11 presentation of data: how is a frequency polygon drawn
what is an ogive and how is it constructed
can a histogram be drawn for unequal class intervals discuss
draw a frequency polygon for the given distribution
which graph would you use to read the number of observations below a value

solution_steps.explain: Erect rectangles on class intervals with heights equal to frequencies, keeping no gaps between them.
Join the mid-points of the rectangle tops with straight lines, closing on the axis at both ends.
Plot running totals of frequencies against class boundaries and join -- the rising ogive shows counts below any value.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A family's monthly spending is {component} on food out of a total of {total}. Find the angle for food in a pie chart.
In a survey of {total} students, {component} prefer cricket. Compute the pie chart angle for cricket.
